text: PGBank partners with IFC to expand trade finance operations

HÀ NỘI - PGBank has signed an agreement with the International Finance Corporation (IFC) to join its Global Trade Finance Program (GTFP), aiming to expand access to trade finance for import-export businesses.
The GTFP is an IFC initiative that connects banks in emerging markets with a global network of international financial institutions through guarantees covering trade finance transactions.

The programme aims to strengthen participating banks' capacity to provide trade finance, enabling businesses, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), to access the financing needed to participate in international trade.
Under the agreement, PGBank becomes an issuing bank under the GTFP, joining 11 other Vietnamese joint-stock commercial banks participating in the programme.
The partnership will enable PGBank to broaden its relationships with leading international financial institutions and strengthen its presence in international financial markets.

Nguyễn Văn Hương, Chief Executive Officer of PGBank, said the partnership with IFC through the GTFP marked an important milestone in the bank's strategy to expand its international financial connections and strengthen its trade finance capabilities.

"With IFC's global network and extensive experience, we expect this programme to provide further momentum for the development of our trade finance operations while enabling us to deliver more effective financial solutions to customers, particularly import-export businesses and SMEs," Hương said.

Speaking on behalf of IFC, Allen Forlemu, Regional Industry Director for the Financial Institutions Group in Asia and the Pacific, highlighted the important role of SMEs in Việt Nam's economy, noting that many businesses continued to face difficulties accessing trade finance.
"Through our partnership with PGBank, IFC aims to help bridge this financing gap, enabling more businesses to access finance and participate more deeply in global supply chains," Forlemu said.
PGBank is pursuing a digitally driven retail banking strategy focused on individuals, households and SMEs, particularly those operating in manufacturing, business and trade.
The bank plans to further diversify its financial services to support businesses in their import-export activities and help Vietnamese enterprises access international markets.
Joining the GTFP is expected to strengthen PGBank's capacity to provide trade finance services while expanding its network of international financial partners.

The partnership follows Moody's first credit assessment of PGBank, which assigned the bank a standalone Baseline Credit Assessment (BCA) of b1 and a long-term deposit rating of B1, with a stable outlook.
